evidence: src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts, cancel-order-use-case.ts, list-orders-use-case.ts and place-order-use-case.ts all return results through toOrderDto from src/application/order-mapper.ts.
src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts and src/application/list-orders-use-case.ts both validate status through the domain's isOrderStatus, so the status rule lives in one place.
src/application/cancel-order-use-case.ts and src/application/place-order-use-case.ts both go through StockAllocationService (release/reserve) instead of changing product stock directly.
src/application/get-stock-levels-use-case.ts maps products to StockLevelDto inline. This is the only place that mapping exists, so nothing is duplicated.
src/application/order-dto.ts declares StockLevelDto next to the order DTOs. The file name is a small mismatch, not a split in concerns.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is one cohesive application layer for order fulfilment. It holds five use cases, a shared DTO file and one mapper. All four order use cases follow the same pattern. They take domain repository and service ports through the constructor, delegate state changes to the Order aggregate, and return results through the shared toOrderDto mapper, so no use case builds OrderDto by hand. Status validation is not duplicated: AdvanceOrderUseCase and ListOrdersUseCase both call the domain's isOrderStatus. The not-found guard repeated in AdvanceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase is a one-line lookup check, not a business rule, so it does not count as a duplicated invariant. There are two small style issues, and neither breaks a rule or invariant. First, GetStockLevelsUseCase maps products to StockLevelDto inline rather than through a mapper, but that mapping exists only in that one file. Second, StockLevelDto is declared in order-dto.ts even though it is about stock, not orders. Neither splits the module into unrelated concerns or bypasses its abstractions.
